# tosi-svg-gltf

<!--{"pin":"top","order":1}-->

**SVG textures inside glTF/GLB, rasterized by the viewer at the resolution it needs.**

A 2048 × 2048 texture is 16 MB of GPU memory and, as a PNG, often a megabyte
or more of download. The SVG it was drawn from is usually a few kilobytes.
This project ships the SVG in the model and draws it on the device: as sharp
as that device can show it, no larger than it can afford.

It has two halves that share one small [format](/format/):

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **[Blender add-on](/blender/)** | Import an SVG as an image texture. Blender shows a rasterized preview, and glTF export writes the SVG itself plus a tiny placeholder PNG. [**Download**](/blender/) |
| **This package** (`tosi-svg-gltf`) | A Babylon.js glTF loader extension that finds those SVGs and rasterizes them at the size you choose, plus an engine-agnostic core for anything else. |

A file written this way is still **valid glTF 2.0**. A viewer that has never
heard of it shows the placeholder, a 64 px thumbnail by default.

## Use it with tosijs-3d or Babylon.js

```sh
bun add tosi-svg-gltf
```

```ts:static
import { registerSvgExtension } from 'tosi-svg-gltf/babylon'

// Once, before loading models. Every glTF loader path picks it up,
// including tosijs-3d's b3dLoader and LoadAssetContainerAsync.
registerSvgExtension({
  scale: 1, // × the size the author chose in Blender
  maxResolution: 2048, // and never more than this per side
})
```

That's all. A live example is on the [babylon](/babylon/) page.

`@babylonjs/core` and `@babylonjs/loaders` 9.x are peer dependencies of the
`/babylon` entry only. The package root (`tosi-svg-gltf`) has no dependencies
and does not import Babylon.

## Anything else

The root export is the engine-agnostic part:

- [`readSvgPayload(image)`](/payload/): the SVG payload on a glTF image, or `null`;
- [`textureSize(payload, { scale, maxResolution })`](/payload/): the size to draw it at;
- [`sizeSvg(svg, width, height)`](/size-svg/): set an SVG's pixel size, scaling its content;
- [`svgToCanvas(svg, width, height)`](/hydrate/): rasterize onto a canvas, e.g. for a three.js `CanvasTexture`.

## Why not just export a big PNG?

- **Size on the wire.** Line art, UI panels, labels, diagrams and decals are
  tiny as SVG and large as bitmaps.
- **Memory on the device.** The viewer chooses: 512 px on a phone, 4096 on
  a desktop, the same file for both.
- **Sharpness.** Text and hairlines stay crisp at whatever size you draw them.

It is the wrong tool for photographs, painted textures and noise: anything
that isn't already vector art.

## Develop

```sh
bun install
bun start            # doc site + dev server on https://localhost:8034
bun test             # unit tests
bun blender          # Blender extension: fetch wheels, build the zip, test in Blender
```

See [CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/tonioloewald/tosi-svg-gltf/blob/main/CLAUDE.md)
for how the pieces fit together.

# Blender add-on **SVG Textures for glTF** lets you use an SVG file as a texture in Blender and export it to glTF/GLB **as the SVG itself**. A viewer that supports it draws the texture sharp at whatever size it needs. Everything else still sees an ordinary (small) image. ## Download

⬇ Download tosi_svg-0.1.0.zip

Version 0.1.0 · 7.7 MB · Blender 4.2 or later · Windows, macOS and Linux in one file. The download is large because it carries the SVG renderer ([resvg](https://github.com/linebender/resvg)) for every platform. Blender installs only the one for your computer. ## Install 1. Download the `.zip` above. **Don't unzip it.** 2. In Blender, open **Edit → Preferences → Get Extensions**. 3. Click the **⌄** menu at the top right and choose **Install from Disk…** 4. Pick the `.zip`. "SVG Textures for glTF" appears under **Add-ons**, enabled. You can also drag the `.zip` onto Blender's window. ## Use it ### Import an SVG **File → Import → SVG as Texture (.svg)**, or in the Image Editor, **Image → Open SVG as Texture…** | Option | What it does | | --- | --- | | **Resolution** | The longest side, in pixels. This is the size Blender previews it at, and the size a viewer draws by default. | | **Add to Active Material** | Adds an Image Texture node to the selected object's material (making one if needed), connected to Base Color. | | **Connect Alpha** | Also connects the texture's transparency to the material's Alpha. | The result is a normal image texture. Paint with it, bake with it, render it in Eevee or Cycles. The only difference is that it remembers the SVG it came from. > Blender's built-in **File → Import → Scalable Vector Graphics** is a > different thing: it turns an SVG into curves (3D geometry). Use this add-on > when you want the SVG as a *texture*. ### Change it With the image showing in the **Image Editor**, or its Image Texture node selected in the **Shader Editor**, press **N** for the sidebar. The **SVG Texture** panel is under the **Image** tab (Image Editor) or the **Node** tab (Shader Editor): - **Resolution:** redraws the preview at a new size. This also sets the default size viewers draw it at. - **Fallback Size:** the thumbnail stored for viewers that don't read SVG (default 64 px). Set to 0 to store a single transparent pixel instead. - **Reload SVG:** re-reads the file after you've edited it in Illustrator, Inkscape, Figma… - **Convert to Bitmap:** forgets the SVG. The image then exports as a normal PNG. ### Export **File → Export → glTF 2.0** as usual, as `.glb` or `.gltf`. No options to set. Each SVG image is written as: - the SVG text, in the image's `extras`; - a placeholder PNG where the pixels would have gone. Check the console after exporting: any image the add-on could not convert is named there, and it exports as an ordinary bitmap instead. ## What works, what doesn't **Works:** shapes, paths, strokes, gradients, patterns, clipping, masks, opacity, transforms, embedded (`data:`) images, and text in fonts installed on the viewer's device. **Watch out for:** - **Text.** A viewer draws text with *its* fonts. If the font isn't installed there, it falls back to another and the layout shifts. For anything that must look exact (logos, labels), **convert text to outlines / paths** in your vector app before saving the SVG. - **Linked files.** An `` that points at another file will not be found by the viewer. Embed it, or don't use it. - **Filters and blend modes** can differ slightly between Blender's preview (resvg) and a web browser. - **Scripts, animation and interactivity** are ignored. A texture is a still image. - **One image per texture.** If Blender's exporter has to *combine* images into one (e.g. a color from one image and alpha from another), that texture exports as a bitmap. - **UDIM tiles** are not supported. ## Viewing the result Any glTF viewer opens the file and shows the placeholder. To see the SVG at full sharpness the viewer needs SVG support: [tosijs-3d](https://3d.tosijs.net) and any Babylon.js app using [this package](/babylon/) have it. ## Troubleshooting **"The SVG renderer (resvg) is not available."** The add-on was installed without its renderer. Install it from the `.zip` above, not from a folder or a single `.py` file. **The import menu item is missing.** Check **Edit → Preferences → Add-ons**: "SVG Textures for glTF" must be enabled. **My exported file is still big.** Something else in the scene is large. Check the console for the add-on's messages, and make sure the texture was imported with this add-on: its sidebar panel shows the SVG's size in bytes.

text: # size-svg `sizeSvg(svg, width, height)` returns the SVG with its root element's `width` and `height` set to that many pixels, so a browser decodes it at the size you are about to draw it. That matters because a browser hands an SVG `` to WebGL at its **intrinsic** size: an icon authored as `width="24" height="24"` becomes a 24 px texture however large it is drawn. The edit is textual and works without a DOM, in a worker too: - if the root has no `viewBox`, one is added from its original `width` and `height` (px, pt, pc, mm, cm, in or unitless), so the drawing **scales** to the new size instead of being cropped to it; - `width` and `height` are replaced, or added; - nothing else in the document changes. ```test import { sizeSvg } from 'tosi-svg-gltf' test('an icon is scaled, not cropped', () => { const out = sizeSvg('', 512, 512) expect(out.includes('viewBox="0 0 24 24"')).toBe(true) expect(out.includes('width="512"')).toBe(true) }) ```
title: size-svg

text: # hydrate `svgToCanvas(svg, width, height)` rasterizes SVG text onto a new canvas of exactly that size. It is the engine-agnostic half of the library: anything that can make a texture from a canvas (three.js `CanvasTexture`, a raw WebGL `texImage2D`, a 2D game) can use it. The [Babylon adapter](/babylon/) does **not** go through it: it hands the sized SVG to Babylon's own image loader, which keeps the glTF sampler, mipmaps and orientation exactly as for a PNG. ```js import { svgToCanvas } from 'tosi-svg-gltf' const svg = `` const small = await svgToCanvas(svg, 16, 16) const large = await svgToCanvas(svg, 256, 256) small.style.width = large.style.width = '128px' small.style.imageRendering = 'pixelated' preview.append(small, large) ``` The left canvas is the same SVG drawn at 16 px, the right at 256 px. A texture made from an SVG is only as sharp as the size you rasterize it at. That size is what the [Babylon adapter](/babylon/) chooses per device. ## How it decodes The SVG goes into a `Blob`, then an ``, and `img.decode()` resolves once the browser has it ready to draw. `createImageBitmap(blob)` would be the obvious off-thread route, but browsers refuse SVG blobs there (they reject with "the source image could not be decoded"), so this library does not try it. An SVG drawn as an image **cannot run script or fetch anything**: browsers treat it as an isolated, static document. That is the security model for loading an SVG from a model file you did not author, and it is also why a web font the page has loaded does not reach the texture. Use system fonts, or convert text to paths before export.
title: hydrate

text:
# babylon

`registerSvgExtension(options?)` teaches Babylon's glTF loader to read SVG
textures. Call it once, before loading: every glTF/GLB loaded afterwards,
by any API (`LoadAssetContainerAsync`, `ImportMeshAsync`, tosijs-3d's
`b3dLoader`, …), gets its SVG images rasterized at the size you choose.

```js
import { b3d, b3dLight, b3dLoader } from 'tosijs-3d'
import { orbitCam } from 'tosijs-3d/demo-utils'
import { registerSvgExtension } from 'tosi-svg-gltf/babylon'

registerSvgExtension({ scale: 2 })

preview.append(
  b3d(
    {
      sceneCreated(el) {
        orbitCam(el, { alpha: Math.PI / 2, beta: Math.PI / 2.4, radius: 3.2, target: [0, 0, 0] })
      },
    },
    b3dLight({ intensity: 1.2 }),
    b3dLoader({ url: '/samples/svg-plane.glb' }),
  )
)
```
```css
tosi-b3d { width: 100%; height: 100%; }
```
```test
// LINE COMMENTS ONLY in a fence: a block comment would end the doc comment.
// This fence must stay ADJACENT to the example above: waitFor searches that
// example's preview, and prose between the fences makes them two examples.
const el = await waitFor('tosi-b3d', 30000)
for (let i = 0; i < 600 && !el.scene; i++) await waitMs(50)
let texture = null
for (let i = 0; i < 600 && !texture; i++) {
  texture = el.scene.textures.find((t) => t.name.startsWith('tosi-svg-sample') && t.isReady())
  if (!texture) await waitMs(50)
}

test('the SVG texture loaded at the requested size, not the placeholder', () => {
  expect(Boolean(texture)).toBe(true)
  // authored at 1024 × 1024, registered with scale: 2
  expect(texture.getSize()).toEqual({ width: 2048, height: 2048 })
})
```

That model was exported from Blender by this repo's own test (see
[Blender](/blender/)). Its image holds about 1.4 KB of SVG and a 64 px
placeholder PNG. Zoom in: the edges stay sharp at the 2048 px it was
rasterized at, which is twice what the author set.

## Options

| option | default | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scale` | `1` | Multiplies each image's authored size. `0.5` on a phone, `2` for a close-up. |
| `maxResolution` | `4096` | No side exceeds this, or the GPU's own limit if lower. |
| `resolve` | — | `(payload, image) => ({ width, height })` to choose per image; overrides both. |

`scale` and `maxResolution` can also be functions of nothing, read at each
load, so one registration can follow a quality setting.

## How it works

The extension's `onLoading` hook runs before any material loads. For each
image carrying a [payload](/payload/), it:

1. computes the target size,
2. sets the SVG root's `width`/`height` to it ([sizeSvg](/size-svg/)),
3. sets the image's `mimeType` to `image/svg+xml` and pre-seeds its data
   with the SVG bytes, so the placeholder PNG is never read.

Babylon then loads the texture exactly as it would a PNG. The sampler (wrap,
filtering, mipmaps), `texCoord`, `KHR_texture_transform`, sRGB handling,
naming and asset-container ownership are all Babylon's own code path. There
is no `DynamicTexture` and no second copy of the loader's logic.

Images without a payload are untouched. An SVG the browser cannot decode
fails the load, exactly as a corrupt PNG would.

`unregisterSvgExtension()` removes it.

text: # The format **Version 1.** This is the contract between an exporter (the [Blender add-on](/blender/)) and a viewer ([this package](/babylon/)). It is small on purpose, so other exporters and viewers can implement it. ## Where the SVG goes On a glTF `image`, under `extras.tosi_svg`: ```json { "images": [ { "name": "label", "mimeType": "image/png", "bufferView": 4, "extras": { "tosi_svg": { "version": 1, "svg": "", "width": 1024, "height": 512 } } } ] } ``` | field | type | meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `version` | integer | `1`. A reader ignores a payload whose version it does not know. | | `svg` | string | The complete SVG document. | | `width`, `height` | integer ≥ 1 | The **authored resolution**: the raster size the author previewed it at, and the texture's aspect ratio. | The image's `uri` or `bufferView` holds a **placeholder** PNG: a small thumbnail of the SVG, or a 1 × 1 transparent pixel. It exists so the file is valid glTF 2.0 and so viewers without support show something. ## Why `image.extras`, and not a vendor extension - **On the image, not the texture or textureInfo:** several textures and materials can share one image, so the SVG is stored once. The original plan put it on `textureInfo`, which repeats it per material slot. - **`extras`, not `extensions`:** `extras` needs no `extensionsUsed` entry, draws no "unsupported extension" notice from validators, and Blender's exporter can write it from any image hook without registering an extension. The cost is that nothing declares the file uses it, so a reader has to look at each image. That's cheap. If this is ever proposed as a `KHR_`/`EXT_` extension, the payload moves to `images[i].extensions.` unchanged. ## Reading it 1. For each image, read `extras.tosi_svg`. Treat it as absent unless `version` is known, `svg` is a string containing an ``'s `width`/`height` to the raster size first (adding a `viewBox` from the original size if it has none). A browser uploads an SVG image to WebGL at its intrinsic size, not the size you draw it. [`sizeSvg`](/size-svg/) does this. ## Security Treat `svg` as untrusted input, as you would any image in a file you did not author. Rasterized as an image (``, `createImageBitmap`, resvg), an SVG cannot run script or load external resources. **Never insert it into the DOM as markup.** ## Writing it 1. Store the SVG text verbatim. 2. `width`/`height`: the size the author chose, aspect ratio matching the SVG's viewport. 3. Replace the image's pixels with a placeholder PNG, set `mimeType` to `image/png`, and keep everything else about the image, texture and sampler unchanged.

# Changelog

<!--{"pin":"bottom","order":2}-->

All notable changes to this project are documented here, in
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) format. The npm
package and the Blender extension share one version number.

## Unreleased

## 0.1.0

First version.

### Added

- **Format v1:** `images[i].extras.tosi_svg = { version, svg, width, height }`
  plus a placeholder PNG ([the format](/format/)).
- **`tosi-svg-gltf/babylon`:** `registerSvgExtension({ scale, maxResolution, resolve })`,
  a Babylon.js 9 glTF loader extension that rasterizes SVG images at the
  chosen size through Babylon's own texture path.
- **`tosi-svg-gltf`:** the dependency-free core: `readSvgPayload`,
  `textureSize`, `sizeSvg`, `svgToCanvas`.
- **Blender extension `tosi_svg` (Blender 4.2+):** import SVG as texture,
  resolution and fallback controls, reload, and glTF export of the SVG
  with a 64 px placeholder. Bundles resvg-py 0.5.0 wheels for Windows,
  macOS and Linux (x64 and arm64).
title: Changelog
